verify_reasons: Legal dimension limits are statutory and high-confidence; the escort matrix here is a regional planning default (NOT read from this state's manual) and fees are not codified — confirm the exact escort thresholds, superload definition, current fee schedule and movement curfews with the state permit office before dispatch.
Texas uses TxPROS with weight-based fee tables and a superheavy tier (>254,300 lbs); confirm fee, escort and route/bridge review in TxPROS.

superload_thresholds.note: Texas 'superheavy/superload' handled via TxPROS with route/bridge analysis; loads over 200,000 lbs (and very large dimensions) require engineering review. Over 254,300 lbs gross triggers the superheavy process. Confirm exact tier in TxPROS.

width.note: regional planning default: 1 pilot for over-12' width (front on 2-lane, rear on divided) — confirm exact trigger with the state
regional planning default: 2 pilots for extreme width — confirm with the state

height.note: regional planning default: height pole / pilot when over ~14'6" — confirm with the state

length.note: regional planning default: rear escort for long overall length — confirm with the state

single_trip.fee_formula: Texas single-trip and overweight fees are set by TxDMV schedules (base permit + weight tables + possible county/highway-maintenance fees); quote through TxPROS.
single_trip.note: Single-trip OS/OW permit available; fee not codified here — quote through the state permit portal.

annual.note: Annual/blanket permits available for qualifying divisible or repetitive moves; fees vary — see portal.

movement_restrictions: Typical daylight-only movement (about 1/2 hour before sunrise to 1/2 hour after sunset) for oversize loads — confirm exact hours and any weekend/holiday curfews with the state.
notes: State-level rules only — county/city permits, bridge-specific engineering and low-clearance routing are out of scope. Knowledge-based entry pending point verification against the state manual.
